bounty.barrier: The signup form needs actual screen-reader announcement and runtime keyboard navigation verified.
bounty.criteria: Demonstrate actual screen-reader output and runtime keyboard navigation of the retained email input. Source HTML alone must not be treated as proof of these runtime behaviors.

history.reason: The barrier and criteria explicitly require demonstration of actual screen-reader announcement and runtime keyboard navigation — behaviors that cannot be proven from static HTML alone. The repair HTML does add a programmatically associated label (<label for="email">Email address</label> matching input id="email"), which is a meaningful structural improvement over the baseline's label-less placeholder-only input. The report also honestly scopes its claim to source HTML label association only, making no runtime claims. However, the stated criteria demand verified runtime screen-reader output and keyboard navigation evidence, which neither the HTML nor the report provides. Per the assessment rules, runtime behavior is unobservable from markup alone, so a RESOLVED verdict is not warranted. The feature is retained and the HTML fix is real, but the specific evidentiary bar set by the criteria
Unresolved candidate released; its commitment remains consumed.
